title: He struggled to read. Then he built a reading app used by millions
disclosure: AFFILIATE LINK IN DESCRIPTION - AI VOICE

scenes.label: AWARD NIGHT
scenes.narration: June 2025. Apple names its design award winners, and the inclusivity award goes to an app made by a man who, as a child, struggled to read.

title: THE BOY WHO
LEARNED BY LISTENING
scenes.subtitle: THE SPEECHIFY STORY
scenes.narration: This is the story of Speechify, and of Cliff Weitzman, the boy who found a way around reading.

scenes.label: CLASSROOM
scenes.narration: Cliff struggles with reading for years. In third grade, he is diagnosed with dyslexia. He later called that diagnosis the best day of his life.

scenes.label: BEDROOM
scenes.narration: Why? Because now he knows what is going on. He wants to read Harry Potter, but it is too hard. So he turns to the audiobook.

scenes.label: BEDROOM
scenes.narration: Cliff says he listened to it twenty-two times in a row. Listening becomes his way to learn, even his way to learn English.

scenes.label: HIGH SCHOOL
scenes.narration: As a teenager, he moves to the United States. He takes hard classes, and he says some teachers and staff believed dyslexia was a myth.

scenes.label: BROWN UNIVERSITY
scenes.narration: Then comes Brown University. The reading lists are huge, and Cliff cannot keep up. Reading with his eyes is just too slow.

scenes.label: DORM ROOM
scenes.narration: So at Brown, he writes code: a small program that reads any text out loud, so he can listen to his course readings instead.

scenes.label: SIDE PROJECT
scenes.narration: He builds it for himself first. Then he turns it into Speechify, an app for anyone who would rather listen than read.

scenes.label: BIG NEWS
scenes.narration: January 2017. Forbes puts Cliff on its 30 Under 30 list, for building text to speech that helps people like him.
But there is a big problem. Phones and computers already have free text to speech built in. Why would anyone pay for another reading app?

scenes.label: VOICE LAB
scenes.narration: Speechify bets on doing it better: natural AI voices, faster listening speeds, and reading from PDFs, web pages and even photos of paper pages.
Speechify spreads to phones, computers and web browsers. Students, busy professionals and people with dyslexia start listening instead of reading.

scenes.label: SERVER ROOM
scenes.narration: By 2025, Speechify says it has more than fifty million users, from students to busy professionals.

scenes.label: AWARD NIGHT
scenes.narration: And in June 2025 comes the moment we started with: the Apple Design Award for inclusivity.
Today Speechify calls itself a voice AI assistant, for work, school and fun. The tool one student built for himself now reads to millions.

scenes.label: YOUR DESK
scenes.caption: TRY IT FREE
scenes.narration: So how can you use it? Speechify has a free version. Open a web page, PDF or document, and it reads it out loud with standard voices.
